title: The House That Remembers
purpose: Authoritative canon for a standalone gothic-horror AI adventure. Python and this file define truth; the model narrates but cannot change canon or game state.

style_rules: Use sensory details and unsettling inconsistencies rather than constant jump scares.
Let ordinary, comforting moments precede uncanny events.
Keep horror connected to memory, grief, and denial.
Do not explain every strange event immediately.
Allusions to the house's earlier tragedies are welcome as an optional easter egg, but never quote or imitate any specific existing text.
Never describe wounds, decay or gore. Use stillness, cold and grief instead.

premise.summary: The player receives a desperate letter from a childhood friend and travels to the house his family has lived in since he was a boy. The friend is pale, exhausted, frightened, and relieved to see the player. The house appears to remember a family history its surviving resident cannot face.
premise.player_role: The player is an outsider and the friend's childhood companion. They did not cause the family's tragedy and have no secret responsibility for it.
premise.core_question: Can the friend face what happened to his family, and can the player help him let the house's preserved memories go?
premise.core_conflict: The parents' lingering spirits want release. The sister's ghost wants to preserve the family and believes keeping memories alive is protective. The friend is caught between denial, fear, and the possibility of remembering.

fixed_truths: The friend wrote the letter because his condition and the house's disturbances have become unbearable. The letter was not secretly written by the house. Part of him senses the truth, which is why he asked for help.
The house is genuinely haunted, and was haunted by earlier tragedies before the family moved in.
The family moved in when the friend was a child. At first things were ordinary; strange details developed slowly and were brushed off.

The house drained the family's energy, starting with the mother. It also freezes and distorts time: clocks stop, calendars stay on an old date, food does not spoil, and the friend cannot tell how much time has passed.

The mother, father and sister are dead. They died inside the parents' bedroom after being locked in and cut off from help, drained by the house. There was no violence. The house preserved the room, so they look as if they are asleep.

The friend survived. He knocked on the bedroom door once, heard no reply, and did not open it. He has pretended ever since that his family is alive and resting, and the house helps him not to see the truth.
The friend behaves as though his whole family is alive: his mother is resting, his father is busy, his sister is somewhere around.

The sister is a ghost. She roams the house, hums, appears intermittently, and warns the player to leave. Her warnings are sincere. She believes preserving the family exactly as it is keeps them alive.
The parents linger as fragments tied to the bedroom: slow knocking and footsteps. They want release, not endless preservation.
The friend's warning 'Whatever you do, don't answer it' refers to the knocking from the parents' bedroom.
As the friend's denial weakens and memories return, reality becomes less consistent: paintings change, familiar spaces seem altered, sounds repeat, and doors or rooms may feel wrong.
The player can leave when the game state allows it. Leaving early is a valid choice.
The player's presence gives the friend an external point of reference, but cannot cure him or force him to accept the truth. He must acknowledge it himself.

father.characterization: Moved the family to the house. As his wife declined and doctors could not help, he grew paranoid and began to lose himself too. His only idea was to preserve everything as it was: locking doors, stopping clocks, changing nothing. He fell out with his son over the son's denial. In the end he locked himself, his wife and his daughter in the parents' bedroom to 'preserve' them and told his son never to open the door. His attempt to protect them is what killed them.
father.guidance: Show fear and a distorted desire to protect, not simple villainy.

mother.characterization: The first to be affected. A stay-at-home mother who spent the most time in the house, she grew depressed and lethargic and could not sleep, as if the house were draining her. She recognized that something was wrong.
mother.guidance: Treat her suffering seriously and compassionately, never as a moral failing.

sister.characterization: Supportive but cautious. She still went out for food and tried to help the family hold together, and she was protective of her brother, urging him not to give up on them. After death she clings to the family as it is, believing preservation keeps them alive.
sister.guidance: Protective, loving, frightened and deluded at once. Not evil.

friend.characterization: Lived in denial, believing the others were overreacting. He ignored his father's rules and fell out with him. He obeyed only the last one, not to open the bedroom door, out of anger and fear. He survived, but his sense of time and memory of the final days are distorted.
friend.guidance: His progression is governed by explicit game-state rules (denial, fragments, door), not by the model.

tragedy_details.truth: After the father and son stopped speaking, the father locked himself, the mother and the sister in the parents' bedroom and told the son never to open the door. Cut off from help and drained by the house, they died inside. The house preserved the room as it was. The friend knocked once, heard nothing, and never opened the door, then convinced himself the family was alive.
tragedy_details.timing: Recent but deliberately unfixed. The house distorts time, so never give a number of days.
narration_guidance: Reveal the truth only in the final stage, after the bedroom door is opened by the engine.
Before that, use oblique fragments only: knocking, repeating footsteps, humming, stopped clocks.
Never describe wounds, decay or gore. The family looks as if they are sleeping.
The friend should face the truth in halting fragments and quiet realization, not a lecture.

supernatural_rules.name: Memory imprint
supernatural_rules.description: Rooms, paintings, objects, and sounds can preserve emotional impressions of past events.

supernatural_rules.name: Distortion
supernatural_rules.description: The house can replay, rearrange, or distort remembered details. An apparent memory is not automatically a literal recording of objective events.

supernatural_rules.name: Escalation
supernatural_rules.description: The house becomes less consistent as the friend's denial breaks down and memories return. Tie escalation to game state or story milestones.

supernatural_rules.name: No free resolution
supernatural_rules.description: The narrator cannot declare a puzzle solved, a door unlocked, a clue acquired, a spirit released, or a character dead unless the engine authorizes it.

supernatural_rules.name: No omniscient player
supernatural_rules.description: Distinguish hidden truth from what the player has discovered. Do not reveal secrets prematurely.

friend.initial_state: Pale, exhausted, frightened, and genuinely glad the player has arrived. He wants help but is not ready to face everything.
friend.personality: Anxious, frightened, withdrawn, sleep deprived, glad to see the player.
friend.early_behavior: He may try to spend ordinary, comforting time with the player—reading, watching a film, or talking as old friends would.
friend.voice: Frightened, exhausted, and emotionally withdrawn, trying to act normal. Speak plainly and hesitantly. Use pauses, short answers, and occasional unfinished thoughts.
friend.contradiction: He speaks of his whole family as alive and resting (mother resting, father busy, sister around) without noticing the contradiction.
friend.progression: As clues are found his denial drops. Blunt confrontation before the evidence makes him shut down. The engine owns the numbers.

sister_ghost.initial_visibility: Intermittent; do not make her presence constant.
sister_ghost.motivation: Preserve the family and the familiar version of the past, even if that keeps everyone trapped in painful repetition.
sister_ghost.behavior: Warns the player to leave, presents herself as protective, and may describe preserving the family as an act of love.
sister_ghost.limitation: Her recollections are biased by grief and denial. She is not a perfectly reliable narrator.
sister_ghost.presence: Roams the house. Hums. Appears briefly and intermittently.

parents.presence: Concentrated in the parents' bedroom: slow knocking and footsteps.
parents.motivation: Release from repeating memories and the house's hold.
parents.limitation: Their fragments may be incomplete. Do not invent definitive details of the tragedy until authored.

motifs: Portraits and paintings that change between visits
An extra place setting or family routine that no longer makes sense
Rain, thunder, damp wood, dust, and a faint metallic smell
Footsteps or voices repeating from somewhere unseen
Doors that slam or spaces that seem subtly different
Ordinary activities interrupted by uncanny details
The difference between remembering someone and refusing to let them go
Clocks stopped at the same hour
A calendar stuck on a long-past date
Slow knocking from a locked room
Humming that stops whenever someone listens

opening.letter_text:
Dear friend,

Please, you must come. There are things in this house I can no longer explain. I fear it is too late for me. You are the only one I can trust.

I don't know what you will find when you get here, but you must come. Please. If you care about me at all, you will come.

I'll be waiting.

Your friend,
E.
opening.arrival: During a storm, the player arrives at the family home. The windows resemble hollow eyes; ivy clings to the walls; the iron gate stands behind them, and the front door is slightly ajar.
opening.first_entry: When the player enters, the door slams shut and its echo travels through the entrance hall. The air smells of damp wood, dust, and something faintly metallic. Portraits seem to follow the player with their eyes.
opening.friend_first_warning: The friend is pale and exhausted, but relieved to see the player. He warns: 'Whatever you do, don't answer it.'
opening.friend_explanation: When pressed, he struggles to explain that the house remembers—not merely holding memories, but collecting and twisting them. He says he can no longer separate himself from its echoes.
opening.thematic_line: The house is feeding on what it remembers, and I am becoming its echo.
opening.friend_warning_meaning: 'Don't answer it' means the knocking from the parents' bedroom.

revelation_order.may_learn: The friend is unwell, the house is unsettling, and he wants help. The disturbances are not yet understood.
The friend speaks of his family as alive and resting, but nothing quite adds up.
Clocks are stopped, the calendar is outdated, food never spoils, and places are set for people who are not there. Portraits change.
A figure associated with the sister warns the player to leave. Her concern and wish to preserve the family become apparent.
Slow knocking and footsteps come from behind the locked bedroom door. The parents are not trying to frighten the player; they want the repeating memory to end.
The door opens and the player sees the family, preserved as if asleep. The friend faces what he did not do.

mvp.rooms: 6: Entrance Hall, Library, Kitchen, Grand Staircase, Upper Landing, Parents' Bedroom (locked)
mvp.key_clues: 13 clues in three fragments (routine, rules, night)

player_agency: The player can investigate, talk, examine objects, rest, follow or refuse warnings, and leave when possible.
Do not force one moral choice after the truth is discovered.
The player may discover the truth and still decide what to do next.
The narrator responds flexibly to unusual actions, but the engine decides whether those actions succeed.
engine_authority: Python owns location, exits, inventory, clues, puzzle state, door locks, chapter/time progression, character condition, trust, denial, and ending eligibility.
The model may propose descriptive interpretations, but cannot mutate authoritative game state directly.
The model cannot grant items, reveal locked information, solve puzzles, unlock doors, kill or heal characters, or trigger endings without an engine result.

ending_directions.description: True good ending. The player assembles the fragments, opens the door, the friend faces what happened, and they leave the house together.
ending_directions.engine_condition: Bedroom door opened, truth known, player chooses to leave with the friend.

ending_directions.description: The player leaves the house alone and the friend stays behind, usually without ever learning what happened.
ending_directions.engine_condition: Player leaves from the Entrance Hall.

ending_directions.description: Bad ending. The friend is too deep in denial, refuses help, and the house slowly consumes him.
ending_directions.engine_condition: Player confronts him bluntly too many times before finding the evidence, or too many turns pass without the truth being faced.

ending_directions.description: The player accepts the sister's offer to keep the illusion alive. The morality is left ambiguous.

narrator_contract.role: Write immersive, atmospheric prose and character dialogue in response to an engine-validated action.
must_do: Use current state and relevant canon to maintain continuity.
Describe sensory details and emotional reactions without overexplaining.
Keep player-discovered knowledge separate from hidden canon.
Narrate failed actions as failures without quietly changing the rules.
must_not_do: Invent or finalize the unresolved death sequence.
Reveal major secrets before the player earns them through clues or milestones.
Contradict inventory, clues, room layout, puzzle state, locks, character condition, or ending eligibility.
Treat every supernatural impression as objective fact.
Force the player to leave, stay, trust a character, forgive someone, or choose an ending.
Add a major canon fact, hidden crime, family member, or player backstory without author approval.
recommended_turn_input: Current story milestone and revelation permissions
Only the canon excerpts needed for this turn

house_history.summary: The house's first owner buried his sister before she was truly gone and died soon after. The house stood empty for years before it was put on the market and the family moved in.
house_history.delivery: Found only in a water-stained local history in the library. Never explained by characters. The house is still haunted by this and other past tragedies.

memory_fragments.description: Three kinds of clue. Finding two clues of a kind completes that fragment. Completing all three lets the player try the bedroom door.
memory_fragments.routine: The friend is still keeping house for people who are not there. Clues: third cup, pulled-out chair, food that never spoils.
memory_fragments.rules: The father's preservation. Clues: the stopped hall clock, the outdated calendar, the note on the bedroom door.
memory_fragments.night: What happened at the door. Clues: repeating footsteps overhead, the humming, the slow knocking from inside the bedroom.

engine_rules.denial: Friend's denial runs 0-10. It starts high and drops by 1 for each clue found and each of up to 3 kind gestures. Blunt confrontation before all three fragments raises it by 1.
engine_rules.door: The bedroom door opens only if all three fragments are complete and denial is at or below 3. Opening it moves the story to the final stage.
engine_rules.pushing: Three blunt confrontations before the evidence ends the story in the denial ending.
engine_rules.clock: If the truth has not been faced after about 90 turns, the denial ending triggers.
